SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey addresses the CII Financing Summit 2026, in Mumbai, Maharashtra. | Photo Credit: PTI
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is looking to reduce the onboarding time for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to as short as five days, SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Friday (November 20, 2026), speaking at the CII Financing Summit in Mumbai. Speaking about the developments and milestones achieved by the regulator and the Indian equity market, Mr. Pandey said SEBI’s core philosophy is driven by optimum regulation.
He highlighted that SEBI will soon come up with a consultation paper to further simplify ease of investment for FPIs. SEBI is likely to consider the removal of some of the constraints pertaining specifically to India. “The next phase of reforms must enable our capital markets to finance a wider range of businesses, attract longer-term investments and remain resilient as they grow,” Mr. Pandey said.
He underscored the simplification of access to capital and regulatory compliance as one of the top priorities to develop and deepen the capital markets. SEBI has initiated a comprehensive review of the Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR) framework and is also reviewing the Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR) framework. The regulator is also working towards frameworks to eliminate duplicate reporting, simplify compliance and reduce the regulatory burden on listed entities.
“By simplifying procedures and reducing avoidable compliance burdens, we aim to attract a wider pool of international capital and improve financing opportunities for Indian businesses while maintaining investor safeguards,” Mr. Pandey said.
In an effort to deepen the corporate bond market, SEBI has been working in collaboration with the Reserve Bank of India and the Ministry of Finance. The Ministry and the regulators are working towards a market-making framework, or a fixed-income channel framework. The framework is expected to widen bond distribution and issuer outreach programmes. It is also aimed at identifying and addressing challenges and barriers in bond financing, Mr. Pandey said.
“Bond trading is happening in the secondary market. There is also a request for platforms in which secondary trading is happening. But we need to increase secondary trading, particularly when we have facilitated retail investors to take direct bonds. But until trading is developed and there is liquidity, there won’t be enough maturity. To promote secondary trading, we have a market-making framework. You will get to know about its contours. It is a work in progress,” Mr. Pandey told reporters on the sidelines.
